name: Three.js 3D WebGL Library

licensing.notes: Standard MIT license allows commercial use and modification.

rendering_constraints.notes: Verified 2026-11-12 on the M2 render host: hyperframes snapshot and render capture real WebGL pixels (software/hardware GL in the HyperFrames headless Chrome). The figure is a pure function of film time (motion tracks evaluated in one tween's property setter, because HyperFrames seeks with totalTime(t, true), which suppresses GSAP callbacks). projects/lab-3d-motion: 564 frames, 720x1280, capture 25-27 s, first compile 3m53s (Google Fonts fetch, cached afterwards 0.1 s), total 26-46 s. r158 is the last release with a classic global build (prints a deprecation notice). Peak memory was not measured; 1500 is the workspace render budget, not an observation.

justification: EXPERIMENTAL: carries the 3D Tibi (src/studio/kits/fitness/tibi3d.js) because the 2D rig's art swaps pop on curls, presses and raises. Promote to approved after one full 3D film is built, reviewed and passes the fitness rubric. The earlier concerns (memory above 2 GB, frame capture sync unverified) did not materialise on this host.
